messages:
alex: Heads up 10:12 UTC 10: we started seeing OIDC introspection 500s from our resource servers. Error: "introspection: signature verification failed". Spike from 10:11-10:20. Anyone on idp side?

nina: Im on it. We rotated signing alias for id_token at 09:50 yesterday as part of routine rekey. Introspection service should accept tokens signed by new alias but sounds like verification service didn't pick up the new JWKs cache.

kevin: oncall here. Can you paste a failing introspect request/response?

alex: sample (sanitized):
```http
POST /introspect HTTP/1.1
Host: introspect.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{ "token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Imoldnktalias-OLD" }
```
response:
```json
{ "active": false, "error": "signature_verify_error" }
```

devbot: automated alert: introspection-service returned 500 for 87 unique tokens between 2024-04-10T10:11:03Z and 2024-04-10T10:19:58Z. JWK fetch returned 403 from KMS-backed key admin at 09:49:51Z (recent alias rekey).

nina: ok that matches. KMS rotation updated alias name and published new JWK set under /jwks/current. Introspection service caches JWKs hourly. Looks like cache miss + fetch blocked by a transient IAM policy change when rekey occurred. audit-bot, show the KMS rotation + IAM change.

audit-bot: event: KMS alias rotate executed by @nina-admin at 2024-04-09T09:50:12Z. IAM policy change: service-introspect-role temporarily removed from key:get for ~2m. Diff snippet: `- arn:aws:iam::acct:role/service-introspect-role Allow KMS:Decrypt`

alex: that explains signature verify errors. Resource servers saw tokens signed by new key but introspect couldn't fetch the matching JWK (403) and treated tokens as invalid. Impact: short-lived spike, no privilege escalation but auth flows retried.

kevin: mitigation options?

nina: two quick mitigations: 1) re-enable fallback verification using the previous alias's JWK set until all caches refresh (we can temporarily configure introspect-service to accept both alias-a and alias-b), 2) patch introspect to fall back to asynchronous JWK refresh on 403 and return 503 instead of 500 so clients can retry gracefully. I'll push (1) now as hotfix.

kevin: apply hotfix with canary 2% then 25% then 100. I'll run the rollout.

alex: also create a follow-up to harden the IAM change process so KMS rotations don't temporarily remove access. We should require a canary window and automated tests on key access.

nina: hotfix deployed to canary 2% at 10:24 UTC, no errors. Promoting to 25% now.

devbot: telemetry: introspect 500s down to 0 after 10:27 UTC on canary, global error rate dropping.

kevin: promoted to 100% at 10:33 UTC. Monitoring for 15m.

alex: please open SEC-9001: "KMS rekey IAM flaps cause OIDC introspect failures" with owner nina and remediation checklist: ensure IAM perms stability, tolerate dual-alias JWKs for 48h after rotation, add integration test that simulates temporary 403 on JWK fetch.

nina: created SEC-9001 and linked runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example/oidc-key-rotation. Will follow up with postmortem.

alex: also add an alert: > paging when introspect 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m (we want early visibility).

kevin: added alert, loud page channel eng-oncall + eng-security.

alex: thanks all. Lessons: rekeys are safe only if IAM and JWK distribution are atomic; for future we accept both old+new keys for a short window and make introspect return retryable errors when JWK fetch fails. :white_check_mark:
